qt: to the Commission Elena Kountoura (The Left) Subject:

According to a recent Eurostat report, in 2025 Greece recorded the highest percentage of citizens in the European Union who could not afford to participate regularly in leisure activities, at 27.3 %, compared to the European average of 12.1 %1. The inability to afford to participate in such activities limits opportunities for socialisation, sport and cultural participation, affecting quality of life and increasing the risk of social exclusion, especially for the most vulnerable social groups. The same study notes that the inability to afford specific goods or services could be used as a measure of absolute poverty. Given that this figure indicates a high level of material and social deprivation among citizens, and that it is at odds with the objectives of the new European anti-poverty strategy and the European Pillar of Social Rights action plan to combat poverty and social exclusion2, can the Commission say: 1.
What view does it take of this Greek metric, and how does it intend to address this deprivation within the European Semester?

What European funding tools are being used by Greece to address financial barriers to accessing leisure, sports and cultural activities, particularly for economically vulnerable groups, and with what measurable results?

What will be the budget and timetable for the announced ESF+ call for proposals in 2027, and what complementary initiatives is it planning to provide support in this regard to economically vulnerable citizens in Greece?

What is more, according to Eurostat data for 2025, 87.1 % of the population in Greece reported at least some difficulty in making ends meet, compared to the EU average of 42.5 %. At the same time, Greece recorded the third highest rate of severe material and social deprivation in the EU, with 14.9 % of the population affected. Eurostat (2026), Key figures on European living conditions - 2026 edition (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/en/web/products-key-figures/w/ks-01-26-036). The European Pillar of Social Rights action plan sets a target of reducing the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion in the EU by at least 15 million, including at least 5 million children, by 2030.
